exposure: placement of volunteer obstetrician and midwife teams
training and supervision of local staff
outcome: number of women delivering at the hospital
number of referrals of pregnant women
number of referrals of obstetric fistula patients
cohort: Pregnant women delivering at Mota district hospital, a rural hospital in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, serving a population of 1.2 million people.
finding: Placement of volunteer obstetrician and midwife teams, establishment of emergency obstetric care, and training of local staff resulted in increased deliveries at the hospital, decreased maternal mortality (from 7.1% to <0.5%), and decreased obstetric fistulae (from 1.5% to 0.5%).
